title_as_printed: Precuneus-to-hippocampus connectivity links LTP-like plasticity to cognitive function in subjective cognitive decline and mild cognitive impairment

Task_Type.reason: Group differences (ANCOVA/GEE), Spearman correlations and mediation analysis; no classifier.

Category.reason: The primary domain, rs-fMRI effective connectivity (C1), is coded. The second core measure, TMS-iTBS LTP-like plasticity recorded as EMG motor-evoked potentials, is omitted. Whether TMS-EMG belongs in C2 is a judgement (the C2 examples are EEG/MEG/ERP/fNIRS), but the registry codes TMS measures as C2 elsewhere (the P-263 row, Benussi 2021). Neuropsychology (C5) is also secondary.
Category.quote: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) were used to assess long-term potentiation (LTP)-like plasticity and EC involving the amygdala and hippocampus in 34 individuals with SCD, 27 with MCI, and 35 healthy controls (HC).

Sample_N_Approx.quote: 35 participants were assigned to the HC group, 34 to the SCD group, and 27 to the MCI group for final analysis

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Single-hospital cohort (Jiangsu Shengze Hospital, Nanjing Medical University).

notes: For internal consistency the registry could code this C1;C2, since it codes TMS measures as C2 in the P-263 (Benussi 2021) row.
